question: Should Crabbox authorize a scoped test identity and accept the GitHub Codespaces credential, billing, ownership, and destructive-cleanup boundary as a supported built-in provider contract?
rationale: Tests cannot establish how a real scoped GitHub identity, billable Codespace, asynchronous deletion, dirty repository, and local recovery claim interact; granting the codespace scope and accepting that permanent contract require maintainer authority.

options.title: Prove with an isolated identity
options.body: Grant the codespace scope to a dedicated test identity, run the full redacted exact-head lifecycle including dirty retention and confirmed deletion, then approve the provider contract if the evidence is clean.

options.title: Accept without live proof
options.body: Merge based on the current tests and hosted gates while explicitly owning the risk that real authentication or cleanup behavior may differ.

options.title: Pause the provider
options.body: Leave the PR and linked issue open until a maintainer can own credentials, quota, proof, and the long-term provider compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Prove with an isolated identity
recommendation.body: Grant the codespace scope to a dedicated test identity, run the full redacted exact-head lifecycle including dirty retention and confirmed deletion, then approve the provider contract if the evidence is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: This repository member has repeatedly maintained the branch, proof harness, authentication preflight, and explicit merge gate in the discussion.
